## My Reasoning

I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. The North China Plain is wheat-maize country — that's what the soil knows, what the water table can support (barely, these days), and what the market will take. I'm not going to experiment with something unfamiliar at 65.

I farm about 10 mu total. I'll keep 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and leave 2 mu as a kitchen garden and field margin. My son is in Shijiazhuang — I hire machine services for planting and harvest now, which is fine. My back thanks me.

**Wheat (October planting):** I've switched to Jimai 22 over the past several years. Better straw strength, decent disease resistance. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest to work in the stover. Three irrigations: the winter water in November to protect roots from freezing, jointing water in late March, and heading water in April-May. That's what this land needs — I've tried cutting to two and the grain fills poorly. I'll apply herbicide in early winter and spray a fungicide/insecticide mix before heading. Nitrogen in two splits: base at planting, topdress at jointing.

**Summer maize (June planting, no-till):** Straight after combining the wheat. I use Xianyu 335 — proven hybrid, the cooperative sells it, and I've gotten consistent yields. I sow directly into wheat stubble with the seeder, no tillage. Saves moisture, saves days. Maize wants more nitrogen than wheat but I'm careful not to overdo it — the groundwater here is already deep, and I've watched neighbors chase yield with fertilizer and get nothing extra. Two irrigations: one at emergence if it's dry, one at tasseling. Corn borer spray at big bell stage.
